correctness.rationale: For arbitrary strict input rank chambers, the order-statistic operator is a coordinate selector. Decomposing perturbations into path indicator cuts reduces the seminorm to transitions of selected indices across a cut. Within a cut-crossing sliding window, deleting only left observations and adding only right ones makes the number of right samples among the q smallest nondecreasing. For each fixed count k, the left and right kth-order thresholds move in opposite directions, giving at most one within-count switch; total switches at most 2q-1. Reflection of value order yields 2(w-q)+1. An explicit permutation at n=w+1 has exactly 2min(q-1,w-q)+1 switches, and a dyadic epsilon=1/4 single-jump perturbation attains equality without changing selectors. Endpoint extension achieves all n≥w+1. Exact witness tests r=1..64, exhaustive small selector permutations and random two-input checks all passed; finite tests supplement the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: Completes the natural all-rank variation-sensitivity classification of fixed-width order-statistic smoothers, interpolating the known extremal and median cases. It identifies a sharp and nontrivial rank ladder, notably rank two always has factor three even for arbitrarily wide filters while the center has the entire window-width factor. Constructive extremizers clarify two-input instability despite single-input smoothing, with meaningful implications for designing robust rank filters.
